input.content:
# Fix notes: `slugify("Hello,  World!")`

## Root cause

`slugify` replaced each non-alphanumeric character with its own `-` (regex `[^a-z0-9]` with no quantifier). A run of separators like `",  "` turned into `---`, and punctuation at the start or end of the string left `-` there (`"!"` → trailing `-`).

## Fix

In `textutils.py`, the regex is now `[^a-z0-9]+`, so each run of separators becomes a single `-`. The result is then passed through `.strip("-")` to drop leading and trailing hyphens. I also added type hints (`text: str -> str`), as the project conventions require.

## Test

The new file `tests/test_slugify_regression.py` covers:
- `test_regression_collapse_separators`: the reported case, `"Hello,  World!"` → `"hello-world"`.
- `test_regression_strip_edge_separators`: separators at the start and end are removed.
- `test_regression_only_separators`: `"!!!"` and `""` → `""`.
- `test_regression_keeps_digits`: digits are kept (`"Top 10 Tips"` → `"top-10-tips"`).

Run with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.
